findings.reason: The protected choice-mask generator is correct, concise, and output-optimal, but its inner scan declares the explicitly disallowed local name index. The sole inert candidate preserves mask order, pending-run handling, output order, and the solve contract while renaming only that position to i; protected sources remain unchanged.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 320 and its Python generateAbbreviations surface. The Reference preserves nonoverlapping and nonadjacent replacement rules, the valid and invalid demonstrations, any-order output, both source examples, both constraints, and lowercase input.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064380349 and structurally aligned with the protected app-local helper despite legacy List and inferred collection annotations. The candidate changes one local identifier only; every mask decision and flush operation remains identical.

The output-sensitive workload now uses lengths 4, 6, and 8, producing legal 16, 64, and 256-result tiers over a 16x size span so a quadratic-output control can finish. The candidate passes all eight executions at +0.01 relative growth and 1.00x; explicit linear duplicate scanning passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.55.

The Approach exactly describes the candidate's n-bit position choices, delayed count flushing, prevention of adjacent numeric tokens, mask-to-abbreviation bijection, O(n 2^n) output-sensitive time and space, and singleton and repeated-letter behavior.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, including both source examples, both constraints, the source's valid and invalid abbreviation demonstrations, and adjacency and overlap semantics.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact abbreviation sets and order-insensitive validators.
The invented two-letter row is now a trial rather than a source sample, and all formerly hidden three- and four-letter correctness cases are visible.

The one-letter source example covers the minimum length; a ten-letter visible trial exercises multi-digit abbreviation counts, and an independent maximum-length check verified all 32,768 unique outputs for length 15.

Distinct and repeated source letters, fully literal and fully abbreviated forms, separated runs, and adjacent abbreviated positions verify canonical run coalescing without accidental source-letter merging.
Every case uses the duplicate-sensitive unordered-list validator because output order is unrestricted while membership, cardinality 2^n, and uniqueness are required.

A recursive position-choice oracle verified all eight authored results and all three benchmark results; the candidate also matched it for every one- through seven-letter word over {a, b}, totaling 254 words, and every generated abbreviation decoded exactly to its source.
All eight correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 16-, 64-, and 256-result scaling workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
